q.instruction: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
q.passage:
In the younger, western dialects we find no -ar or -er, but -a and -an or -en.

(A) Old Frisian has no reflexive pronoun, but does show sîn as a possessive form for the masculine and neuter singular: alle sîne sîthar ‘all his colleagues’. Like all the Germanic languages except Gothic, Old Frisian shows an intensified demonstrative pronoun: OF masc. thi and this opposite Goth.

(B) Possibly because of the texts in which it is transmitted, Old Frisian shows no dual pronouns, though modern North Frisian dialects have them. As in Old English, in Old Frisian we find third person personal pronouns beginning with h- throughout: 5. Old Frisian does not distinguish the dative and accusative cases in the first and second person singular personal pronouns: 6.

(C) tham and thissem opposite Goth. þaim Verbs 1. Old Frisian does not show a reduplicating class of verbs. Instead we find either a new vowel alternation, or reassignment to the weak class: OF Goth.
